mcqs.question: A developer sets `tabindex="-1"` on a custom error-summary div so it can receive focus programmatically after a failed form submission. What is the effect on the Tab key sequence?
options: It adds the element into the natural Tab sequence at its DOM position
It forces the element to the very front of the Tab sequence, ahead of everything else
It has no effect on tabindex behavior at all — only inline styles change
It removes the element from the Tab-key sequence entirely, while still allowing JavaScript to focus it directly with .focus()
mcqs.explanation: tabindex="-1" specifically excludes an element from being reached by pressing Tab while still allowing programmatic focus via .focus(), which is exactly why it's the standard tool for directing focus to an error summary or a modal heading after a JS-driven UI change. tabindex="0" is what adds an element to the natural sequence, and no positive-number front-of-queue behavior is involved here.

mcqs.question: A screen reader user clicks a link in a single-page app that changes the visible content via client-side routing, with no full page reload. Why might they hear nothing announced about the change?
options: Screen readers cannot detect any DOM changes made by JavaScript
SPAs are fundamentally incompatible with screen readers
Focus never moved after the route change, since there was no full navigation to reset it automatically the way a traditional page load would
The link itself must be missing an href attribute
mcqs.explanation: A full page navigation resets focus to the top of the document automatically; a client-side route change has no equivalent built-in reset, so without deliberate code moving focus (typically to the new page's heading), nothing draws the screen reader's attention to the change at all. Screen readers can detect DOM changes when told to via aria-live, and this isn't a fundamental SPA incompatibility or an href issue.

mcqs.question: In a focus trap implementation, focus is currently on the last focusable element inside an open modal and the user presses Tab (not Shift+Tab). What should happen?
options: Focus should wrap back to the first focusable element inside the modal
Focus should move to whatever element comes next in the page behind the modal
The Tab key press should be ignored entirely with no focus change
Focus should move to the modal's close button specifically, regardless of where it sits in the DOM
mcqs.explanation: A correct focus trap wraps Tab from the last focusable element back to the first one inside the modal, keeping focus contained rather than letting it escape to the page behind. Ignoring the keypress entirely would strand the user, and there's no requirement to specifically target a close button rather than the first focusable element in DOM order.

mcqs.question: A skip link points to `<main id="main-content">` which has no `tabindex` attribute. What happens when a keyboard user activates the skip link?
options: The browser throws a console error and the link does nothing
The page scrolls to #main-content, but focus stays on the skip link, so the user's next Tab press re-enters the navigation instead of the content
It works identically to having tabindex="-1" present
Focus moves correctly into main, but the page fails to scroll there visually
mcqs.explanation: Without tabindex="-1" on the target, the browser scrolls the anchor into view but doesn't move keyboard focus there, since main isn't natively focusable — so the next Tab press continues from wherever focus actually is, typically re-entering the navigation the user just tried to skip. There's no console error here, and the scroll behavior itself isn't the part that breaks.

mcqs.question: A team removes `outline: none` and replaces plain `:focus` styles with `:focus-visible` styles across their component library. What problem does this specifically fix?
options: It fixes color contrast issues on focused elements
It removes focus indication for mouse users entirely, which is the intended behavior
It fixes a screen-reader announcement bug unrelated to visual focus rings
It stops the focus ring from appearing on every mouse click while still showing it for keyboard interaction, avoiding the all-or-nothing choice :focus forced
mcqs.explanation: :focus-visible exists specifically to let browsers apply a heuristic distinguishing keyboard-driven focus from mouse-driven focus, so a team can show the ring only when it's useful (keyboard navigation) without the previous all-or-nothing choice between an ugly ring on every click or no ring at all via outline: none. It has nothing to do with contrast ratios or screen-reader announcements — those are separate concerns from visual focus indication.

mcqs.question: A modal opens, displays correctly, and passes visual QA, but a keyboard-only user reports they can't reach it at all — Tab keeps cycling through elements on the page behind it. What's the most likely root cause?
options: The modal's CSS has a z-index conflict with the page content
The modal is missing an aria-label
Focus was never explicitly moved into the modal when it opened, so keyboard focus stayed wherever it was on the page behind it
The modal's animation duration is too long for the browser to register focus
mcqs.explanation: This is the single most common real-world instance of this bug — the modal opening correctly visually says nothing about whether focus was ever moved into it programmatically, and without that explicit step, Tab continues cycling through whatever was already focusable before the modal appeared. A z-index issue would cause a visual stacking problem, not this one, and neither a missing aria-label nor animation timing explains focus never entering the modal at all.
